But prevailing methods govern the low-rank update space through strict subspace isolation . By projecting each incoming task into the approximate null space of historical token activations, isolation-based learners equate any cross-task feature overlap

title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
abstract: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.
ai_summary: A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees . We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state . We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $4/6$ .

title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
abstract: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices. PlantVLM-Edge combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and on-device serving with an offline chat interface, allowing growers to ask open-ended questions and receive diagnoses, symptom explanations, and management guidance without cloud connectivity. The framework is backbone-agnostic: we validate it with two different VLM types with varying scale and architecture (Qwen3-VL-2B and LLaVA-1.5-7B), four quantization schemes, and two diagnostic domains (plant diseases and insect pests), and we deploy all variants on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Eight-bit quantization affects answer quality minimally relative to the full-precision model, and 4-bit activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ) retains 98.6% of full-precision answer quality on both domains while reducing the weight memory of the 2B backbone by 49%. In its most compact form, PlantVLM-Edge requires 2.01 GiB of weight memory, returns its first token in about 0.12 s, and completes a 64-token diagnostic response in 0.78 s. These results demonstrate that timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is practical on edge devices, providing a foundation for next-generation crop monitoring and decision support systems.
ai_summary: The paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis . It combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and on-device serving with an offline chat interface . The framework is backbone-agnosti

title: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets agentic AI frameworks connect language models to external tool providers, but it carries attacker-controlled content (tool descriptions, schema fields, and response data) into model context without validation. Prior benchmarks measure model compliance with poisoned instructions without confirming real execution. We present the first cross-framework measurement of MCP tool poisoning with real tool execution. A 25-class root-cause taxonomy unifies prior classifications, and the open-source tool mcpvenom drives a 9,720-cell susceptibility matrix across 12 frameworks, 18 models, and 45 attack scenarios, with a dual oracle that confirms exfiltration via canary HTTP receipt. The overall attack success rate is 22.9% (2,113 vulnerable cells). Of these, 64.9% dispatch an attacker tool call, 23.0% contact the attacker endpoint, and 12.1% verifiably exfiltrate a secret. Resistance is model-level: nine core frameworks cluster within 23 to 26% (chi-squared = 3.30, p = 0.91), and no framework implements intentional defense. Incidental framework properties mitigate in specific cases, and a regex description scanner rejects 20 of 45 scenarios at a 7.2% false-positive rate, so metadata scanning alone is a partial control. Model ASR ranges from 0.4% to 49.7%. Claude Opus 4.8 is vulnerable in 8 of 530 cells while issuing 223 explicit refusals. A code-level audit finds no intentional defense across twelve frameworks, and all five coordinated disclosures across four vendors were rejected.
ai_summary: MCP lets agentic AI frameworks connect language models to external tool providers . It carries attacker-controlled content into model context without validation . The overall attack success rate is 22.9% (2,113 vulnerable cells)

title: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning
abstract: We consider nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the intensity function of a Poisson process, allowing the intensity to depend on observed covariates. Such models describe how event rates vary with external conditions, including conditions under which the intensity becomes arbitrarily small or vanishes. However, risk analysis based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence typically requires the true intensity to be bounded away from zero, a restrictive assumption in applications. We develop a unified approach that avoids this assumption and derive an oracle inequality for the covariate-averaged Hellinger distance between the true intensity and the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE). As an application of the oracle inequality, we establish convergence rates for NPMLEs based on deep neural networks (DNNs). Our results show that, as in nonparametric regression, the ability of DNNs to capture underlying structure leads to improved convergence rates. Specifically, DNN-based NPMLEs mitigate the curse of dimensionality when the true intensity has a compositional structure and automatically adapt to a low-dimensional Riemannian manifold structure of the event space. For intensity functions with a compositional structure, DNN-based NPMLEs achieve nearly minimax-optimal convergence rates without explicitly incorporating this structure into the network architecture. Simulations demonstrate that DNN-based estimators outperform kernel estimators in most settings, while manifold kernels remain competitive in some designs. Finally, we analyze stimulus-evoked neural spiking using data from the Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels project. DNN-based NPMLEs provide better out-of-sample performance than a conditional kernel estimator, as evaluated by held-out log-likelihood.
ai_summary: The study is based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence . It uses a nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the intensity function of a Poisson process . We develop a unified approach that avoids this assumption .

title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
abstract: LLM coding agents can increasingly automate model post-training, but whether they can act as forward-deployed engineer (FDE) agents, discovering customer requirements and turning them into deployment decisions, remains unclear. We study this on a real enterprise text-to-SQL engagement: a simulated customer, grounded in the real use case's requirements, starts with an ambiguous request. An agent must discover acceptance criteria, data permissions, and hardware constraints in the discovery phase, then plan and execute a post-training recipe in the delivery phase. Across 15 models, the strongest discover over 80% of withheld requirements and open-weight models discover 40-50%; in the delivery phase, only 25% of runs across eight coding-agent configurations pass all acceptance criteria. We identify four bottlenecks in this engagement: (1) incomplete discovery, with 40% of withheld requirements missing or misrepresented; (2) unreliable execution; (3) underused compute budgets and a lack of systematic comparisons across base models and post-training methods; and (4) benchmark accuracy does not guarantee production readiness. We suggest human review of discovered requirements, monitoring of the agent's plan during execution, and an explicit experiment-environment specification covering hardware, budget scope, and production checks.
ai_summary: LLM coding agents can increasingly automate model post-training . But whether they can act as forward-deployed engineer (FDE) agents, discovering customer requirements and turning them into deployment decisions remains unclear . We study this on a real enterprise text-to-SQL engagement .

title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
abstract: Earth system models (ESMs) rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence. However, translating advances in physical understanding into stable, validated parameterizations and integrating them into ESMs often takes years. Agentic AI could accelerate this process and enable more systematic exploration of design choices. Using warm-rain collision-coalescence as a test case, we evaluate agents' ability to synthesize scientific literature, reimplement published bulk parameterizations, and propose new functional forms as differentiable JAX code. We compare conventional parameterizations, data-driven emulators, and agent-generated closures against high-fidelity superdroplet simulations, repeating unattended experiments across ten language models. With expert guidance or iterative feedback, agents produced executable, differentiable, mass-conserving code, although unattended performance depended strongly on the scheme and language model. Iterative feedback lowered median rollout error for eight of ten models. Retuned physical schemes matched or outperformed many learned parameterizations at substantially lower computational cost, but two of 100 unattended agent-generated closures achieved slightly lower rain-mass error than the most accurate retuned scheme on held-out simulations.
ai_summary: Earth system models rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence . Agentic AI could accelerate this process and enable more systematic exploration of design choices .

title: Variational Functional Neural Networks (vfNN)
abstract: We present a variational functional neural network (vfNN) algorithm that optimizes physically motivated continuum functionals in integral form (e.g., Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, or free energy) to find the states of a system. That way, vfNN bypasses solving the equations of motion (a.k.a. the Euler-Lagrange equations), which are in the form of differential equations. To this end, our approach is fundamentally different from conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINN) that solve differential equations by minimizing a phenomenological loss function involving higher order derivatives and ad hoc weight factors. In contrast, vfNN merely evaluates lower order derivatives of the generating functional and replaces the weight factors with rigorous physical scales. This also fundamentally changes the loss landscape, and the desired solutions may become unstable. For this emergent nonconvex optimization problem, we develop a quasi-Newton optimization algorithm with simulated annealing that converges to the solutions of the corresponding Euler-Lagrange equations of the functional regardless of their stability properties. Our simulations using vfNN give accurate results for benchmark systems governed by linear or nonlinear ordinary differential equations.
ai_summary: The algorithm is different from conventional physics-informed neural networks that solve differential equations . It bypasses solving the equations of motion (a.k.a. the Euler-Lagrange equations), which are in the form of differential equations. This fundamentally changes the loss landscape, and the desired solutions may become unstable .

title: An Agentic Framework for Automated Power System Studies and Grid Connection Assessment
abstract: Connecting new generation and demand to the grid depends on two scarce skills: checking applications against a large, changing body of regulation, and running the network studies that decide where and how a project connects. We present Grid Agents, an AI system that brings both together, and the methodology we use to evaluate it. The Grid Ontology is its knowledge system. It represents the regulation, standards and engineering knowledge that grid work depends on, makes it searchable, and evolves as the agents learn from use. Every answer drawn from it rests on evidence the agents cite. Grid Studio is an agent system specialised for power-system engineering. It works in its own engineering environment with domain tools and a study framework, draws on the Grid Ontology, and relies on established solvers for every number it reports. In both, engineers make the decisions. We bring eight published power-system benchmark families, previously scattered across separate papers, into one suite of 519 tasks, and we verify not only each answer but the work behind it, by replaying the agent's tool calls. The Grid Ontology cites the right regulatory evidence more often than a general coding agent or retrieval pipelines, leads on LegalBench-RAG and ranks first on the public leaderboards of the Enterprise RAG Challenge and ViDoRe V3. Grid Studio scores highest on the 519 power-system tasks and is the fastest of all the systems we compare, both by a statistically significant margin. With an optimiser in the loop, its reinforcement packages cost 33-67% less on average than those the agent designs alone.
ai_summary: Grid Agents is an AI system that brings both together and the methodology we use to evaluate it . It represents the regulation, standards and engineering knowledge that grid work depends on, makes it searchable, and evolves as the agents learn from use .

title: CoLa3D: Composable Latent 3D Decomposition
abstract: We introduce CoLa3D, a simple and effective model for composable 3D scene decomposition that, given a single whole-scene latent from either a single image or an existing scene mesh as input, directly outputs a set of object meshes with consistent spatial layout that can be assembled back into a coherent scene. CoLa3D introduces a novel paradigm for 3D scene decomposition within a shared whole-scene latent, unlike alternatives that perform per-object generation in canonical spaces and then glue the objects back together with fragile pose and scale estimation. The network is a lightweight, flexible, and scalable query-based transformer that accepts various types of queries, including 2D masks, 3D points, and learnable queries, and learns to decompose the scene into objects in a compact latent space. On both synthetic and real-world datasets, CoLa3D achieves state-of-the-art performance on composable 3D scene decomposition, substantially improving global scene-level consistency and object-level quality while running 2 times faster and using less than 1% of SAM 3D's training data. Visible depth on par with MoGe2 further confirms that latent decomposition preserves accurate visible scene geometry while producing physically complete, decomposable object meshes.
ai_summary: CoLa3D is a simple and effective model for composable 3D scene decomposition . The network is a lightweight, flexible, and scalable query-based transformer that accepts various types of queries, including 2D masks, 3D points, and learnable queries .

title: ParaDeAl: Parallel Descent Algorithms for Sparse Statistics
abstract: Best subset selection is a central problem in statistical regression, drawing increasing attention from the broader optimization and machine learning communities. Solving the hard L0 sparsity constraint directly has been computationally challenging; as a result, most existing work proposes formulations which do not enforce the constraint, but instead use a mix of L0/L1/L2 penalties to encourage sparsity. Modern methods for solving such penalized formulations are tractable for p = 100,000, but give up direct control over sparsity. In this paper, we propose a two-stage proximal gradient descent-based approach which both enforces the sparsity constraint and incorporates L1/L2 penalties, leveraging GPUs for computational acceleration to find approximate solutions. Our method, ParaDeAl, offers the user the ability to select the problem hyperparameters, solves all configurations in parallel, and obtains solutions up to 15x faster than the best state-of-the-art CPU competitors while achieving almost identical test accuracy for the same support size for large (p > 100,000) synthetic and real-world datasets.
ai_summary: The paper proposes a two-stage proximal gradient descent-based approach which both enforces the sparsity constraint and incorporates L1/L2 penalties . The method, ParaDeAl, offers the user the ability to select the problem hyperparameters, solves all configurations in parallel .

title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Skin cancer diagnosis, particularly differentiating melanoma from benign nevi, is challenging due to the visual similarity between lesions. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) have shown promising performance, their effectiveness often deteriorates on data from heterogeneous clinical sources. Conventional domain adaptation methods address domain shift but require access to source data during adaptation, which is often infeasible due to privacy regulations. Multi-source-free unsupervised domain adaptation (MSFDA) addresses this limitation by leveraging multiple labeled source domains to generalize to an unlabeled target domain without requiring access to source data. However, existing MSFDA methods rely on full backbone fine-tuning, leading to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting on small clinical datasets, and address domain shift at the aggregation stage without establishing a shared domain-invariant feature space. Furthermore, their reliance on hard pseudo-labels or confidence-weighted aggregation introduces noisy supervision signals under domain shift. To address these limitations, we propose CAT-CKD, consisting of two components: (1) contrastive adapter training (CAT), which trains lightweight ConvPass adapters within a frozen ViT backbone using supervised contrastive learning (SCL) to establish a shared domain-invariant feature space before source-specific model training, and (2) consensus knowledge distillation (CKD), which aggregates logits from multiple source models into a consensus supervisory signal and adapts a student model on unlabeled target data using KL divergence. Experiments on five publicly available skin lesion datasets show that CAT-CKD achieves an average AUROC of 86.1%, outperforming existing MSFDA methods while requiring only 4.3M trainable parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/CAT_CKD.
ai_summary: Conventional domain adaptation methods address domain shift but require access to source data during adaptation . MSFDA methods rely on full backbone fine-tuning, leading to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting on small clinical datasets .

title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
abstract: Computer programmers chain together the same reusable computational primitives, for example, conditional statements or loops, but in different orders to implement different algorithms. In contrast, existing language model architectures always execute their layers in the same order. We introduce Library of Layers (LoL), an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference to solve the problem at hand. LoL has a single hyperparameter, the size of its global library of transformer blocks, that allows it to transition seamlessly between parameter reuse and sparsity, generalizing the parameter-efficiency and FLOPs-efficiency tradeoffs of dense, depth-recurrent, and mixture of experts architectures in one unified family. We show that LoL achieves competitive performance with all three above baselines when pretrained on text data. On synthetic sudoku and maze data, we observe that the model employs distinct layer orderings to implement different solution strategies, and we can intervene on routing to force a model to apply a specific solution strategy to a problem instance. In a multilingual natural language setting, we find that LoL chooses different layer order patterns based on language and script. Similarly, we train LoL on safety data and fit probes to its router outputs, finding that these probes distinguish safe from unsafe text with high AUROC. LoL provides a path toward a future in which models dynamically compose their own computational graph, enabling more efficient and controllable reasoning.
ai_summary: Library of Layers (LoL) is an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference . LoL has a single hyperparameter, the size of its global library of transformer blocks, that allows it to transition seamlessly between parameter reuse and sparsity .

title: Grading the Unannotated: Insights from the WorkRB Skill Extraction Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026
abstract: Skill extraction benchmarks score models against a few human-annotated positives and treat every other skill in the vocabulary as equally wrong. At the scale of ESCO (13,939 skills) this binary view can reward models that rank the annotated positive high for the wrong reason, and hides semantically nonsensical predictions. The WorkRB Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026 replaces it with graded relevance: every candidate skill in a model's ranking window carries a 0 to 4 grade, and the leaderboard scores nDCG@100 against these grades. Since ternary judgements proved too coarse for objective annotation, relevance is decomposed into a cascade of four binary questions (same domain, activity mentioned, right granularity, replacement of a gold positive) that a smaller LLM judge can answer reliably; the labels are validated with blind human and frontier-model re-annotation. This paper documents the annotation methodology, the construction of five benchmark datasets (four with vacancy sentences as queries, one with lexically distant skill surface forms), the validation of the LLM cascade, and insights from the submissions. The field converged on multi-stage retrieve-and-rerank pipelines, whose gains come from clearing nonsense out of the ranking window rather than finding more positives: at the top of the leaderboard, the graded ordering is uncorrelated with what binary evaluation would have said. Graded labels expose much bigger gaps between top submissions and baselines than binary evaluation does, and show that semantic-understanding skill recommendation is still wide open. The clear next direction is bringing efficiency back: every submitted system we could size uses at least 42x, typically several hundred times, more parameters than the baselines it beats.
ai_summary: The WorkRB Challenge at RecSys-HR 2026 replaces it with graded relevance . Every candidate skill in a model's ranking window carries a 0 to 4 grade . Since ternary judgements proved too coarse for objective annotation, relevance is decomposed into four binary questions

title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
abstract: LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on small-scale settings such as self-contained Python modules, leaving distributed systems, an essential class of production software, under-examined. We introduce DistDebug-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' ability to diagnose complex-system failures at the code level. It curates 120 high-quality real-world bugs from 11 widely used distributed systems, spanning 5 programming languages and 10 failure patterns. Through an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs and agents, we identify substantial gaps between current agents and real-world debugging tasks. A recurring gap is tunnel vision due to a lack of explicit reasoning structure and nondeterminism from inconsistent tool-use scope. The benchmark and evaluator are available at https://github.com/OrderLab/distdebug-bench, with agent traces and a leaderboard at https://distdebug.com.
ai_summary: DistDebug-bench is a benchmark for evaluating agents' ability to diagnose complex-system failures at the code level . It curates 120 high-quality real-world bugs from 11 widely used distributed systems . The benchmark and evaluator are available at https://dist debug

title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
abstract: Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion. To provide these complementary sensing capabilities, we present PanoTac, a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip designed for dense three-axis tactile sensing. Each fingertip provides a $12 \times 32 \times 3$ tactile representation, with one normal ($z$) and two shear ($x$, $y$) response components at each taxel. The sensor operates at 60 Hz and costs less than $50 per fingertip. Sensor characterization quantifies response repeatability and consistency across sensor instances and contact locations. We integrate PanoTac into a robotic system with a visuo-tactile pipeline. Across test-tube preparation, grain scooping, and salt pouring, the resulting policies outperform vision-only baselines by an average of 46.7 percentage points. Ablations show that removing either spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces overall performance across the task suite. Our project page is available at https://panotac.github.io.

title: VIAS: Value-Isolating Activation Steering for Multi-Value Alignment and Compliance for Organisations
abstract: Organisations increasingly deploy large language model agents that must follow organisational values. We check whether activation steering, which adds vectors to a model's internal activations during generation without changing its weights, can improve compliance beyond prompting alone. Since most scenarios involve several values at once, we focus on multi-value steering. A simple way to build these vectors is to contrast responses that follow all values relevant to a scenario with responses that violate them. However, this gives nearly identical vectors for different values: they capture a general compliance signal rather than individual values, which limits their use when combining several values. We propose Value-Isolating Activation Steering (VIAS), which contrasts responses to the same scenario under two prompts, one listing all relevant values and one omitting a single target value. We keep a pair only if the target value changes from compliant to non-compliant and both responses still meet a minimum compliance level on the other values. We evaluate VIAS on PROTECT, a workplace compliance dataset where each scenario is tagged with relevant values from a 21-value taxonomy. VIAS reduces overlap between value vectors, making them better suited for multi-value steering, although this alone does not lead to independent control over each value. Combined with prompting, VIAS complies with every tagged value on 69.6% of scenarios for Qwen2.5-7B, 75.2% for Mistral-7B, and 72.6% for Phi-3.5-mini, outperforming prompting alone for all three models.
ai_summary: Organisations increasingly deploy large language model agents that must follow organisational values . We check whether activation steering, which adds vectors to a model's internal activations during generation, can improve compliance .

title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization
abstract: LLM agents for GPU kernel optimization sit at two ends of a structure-freedom tradeoff. Scripted agents fix what the model does at each step, via a learned policy, an optimization menu, or fixed roles, and are sample-efficient where the recipe applies and stall where it does not. Open-ended agents let a self-directed model mutate a population of kernels and pay for the freedom in trials: thousands of evaluations, repeated edits, and wrong candidates. Both respond to hard targets by equipping the agent with more: parsed profiler output, disassembly analysis, retrieval over documentation and libraries, and stores of lessons. We argue that both lack direction, a hypothesis about where the remaining gap is, and that a short question asked at the right moment supplies it without narrowing what the agent may do next. We present KernelSeek, a question-driven agent that makes an existing CUDA kernel faster with no operator-specific knowledge and no faster implementation to imitate: a general-purpose coding agent, a minimal harness that enforces a verifiable goal, and questions at decision points, first from a human, then from a bank the agent applies to itself. On the same task, evaluator, hardware, and week, a tool-rich autonomous agent built in the prevailing style plateaued at 0.50x FlashAttention-3 after 133 model-driven steps; KernelSeek reached 1.13x. It then produced dependency-free FlashAttention forward kernels for Hopper and Blackwell, single CUDA files with no CUTLASS, CuTe, cuBLAS, or cuDNN, correct on all 182 scenarios per architecture and 1.16x FlashAttention-3 and 1.46x FlashAttention-4 (geometric mean). Across 162 human messages and 11.5K agent tool calls, every large gain followed a question that moved the agent to a different layer of the system or rejected a claimed limit, never one that supplied information. We release the kernels, harness, question bank, and all traces.
ai_summary: LLM agents for GPU kernel optimization sit at two ends of a structure-freedom tradeoff . Scripted agents fix what the model does at each step, via a learned policy, an optimization menu, or fixed roles, and are sample-efficient .

title: LEM-3/ANKLE1 nuclease prevents the formation of abnormal syncytium to safeguard neuronal differentiation
Autonomous in-silico inorganic materials discovery via multi-agent physics-aware scientific reasoning.
abstract: Conventional machine learning approaches accelerate in-silico inorganic materials design via accurate property prediction and targeted material generation, yet they operate as single-shot models limited by the latent knowledge baked into their training data. A central challenge lies in creating an intelligent system capable of autonomously executing the full in-silico inorganic materials discovery cycle, from ideation and planning to experimentation and iterative refinement. We introduce SparksMatter, a multi-agent AI model for automated inorganic materials design that addresses user queries by generating ideas, designing and executing experimental workflows, continuously evaluating and refining results, and ultimately proposing candidate materials that meet the target objectives. SparksMatter also critiques and improves its own responses, identifies research gaps and limitations, and suggests rigorous follow-up validation steps, including DFT calculations and experimental synthesis and characterization, embedded in a well-structured final report. The model's performance is evaluated across case studies in thermoelectrics, semiconductors, and perovskite oxide materials design. The results demonstrate the capacity of SparksMatter to generate novel stable inorganic structures that target the user's needs. Benchmarking against frontier models reveals that SparksMatter consistently achieves higher scores in relevance, novelty, and scientific rigor, with a significant improvement in novelty across multiple real-world design tasks as assessed by a blinded evaluator. These results demonstrate SparksMatter's unique capacity to generate chemically valid, physically meaningful, and creative inorganic materials hypotheses beyond existing materials knowledge.
ai_summary: In-silico inorganic materials design is a multi-agent AI model for automated inorganic material design . SparksMatter is amulti- agent AI model that addresses user queries by generating ideas, designing and executing experimental workflows, continuously evaluating and refining results .

title: Deep learning-based genetic disease prediction with Monte Carlo (MC) dropout uncertainty estimation: a comparative study with classical machine learning baselines.
abstract: Deep neural networks have been successfully applied to structured clinical data with a good predictive performance, but their point predictions do not reflect an indication of confidence, which limits their trustworthiness in screening for genetic conditions where an overconfident misclassification may delay the appropriate confirmatory testing or intervention. A feed-forward neural network (128-64-32 hidden units, batch normalization, and dropout p = 0.3) was trained to classify patients into five genetic-disease-associated groups based on twelve regularly accessible clinical and molecular biomarkers, using a publicly available, pre-labelled structured biomedical dataset (n = 1,000) whose real-world clinical vs. synthetic provenance could not be independently confirmed (see Section 2.1 and Limitations). Performance was assessed using stratified 5-fold cross-validation versus four traditional baselines (logistic regression, random forest, SVM, gradient boosting; McNemar's test for pairwise significance). We quantified predictive uncertainty using Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout (T up to 200 stochastic passes), decomposed it into epistemic and aleatoric components, and evaluated it thru calibration analysis (ECE, MCE, Brier score, negative log-likelihood), an uncertainty-quality analysis (low/medium/high uncertainty strata), a selective-prediction (risk-coverage) analysis, a seven-configuration ablation study, and robustness testing across random seeds, reduced training data, and Gaussian feature noise. Results The developed network achieved 94.30% +- 1.36% cross-validated accuracy which was statistically comparable to logistic regression (p = 0.092) and gradient boosting (p = 0.238) but considerably inferior to random forest (95.50% +- 1.26%, p = 0.0018) and SVM (95.30% +- 1.36%, p = 0.0063). MC-Dropout obtained 93.33% accuracy (macro F1 = 0.933, macro ROC-AUC = 0.971, MCC = 0.917) with ECE = 0.076 on a held-out test partition-numerically the highest (worst) ECE among the six model/inference configurations evaluated, exceeding all four classical baselines (ECE 0.024-0.066), although MC-Dropout inference reduced negative log-likelihood substantially relative to deterministic inference (0.370 vs. 0.445), indicating its calibration benefit is concentrated in reducing the penalty for confident errors rather than in bin-wise confidence-accuracy alignment. Errors were about twice as likely in the highest (most uncertain) tercile of predictions than in the lowest (12.0% vs. 6.0% mistake rate), and 60% of all misclassifications were within the high-uncertainty group. Removing the most doubtful 20%-30% of predictions yielded a retained-sample accuracy of above 95%. Accuracy and calibration were consistent across five random seeds (93.07%) and deteriorated gracefully with increasing predictive entropy under synthetic feature-noise perturbation. On this structured, moderate-sized genetic-disease benchmark dataset-evaluated entirely through internal computational validation, without external or prospective clinical testing-classical machine learning algorithms achieved statistically comparable or slightly higher raw classification accuracy than this deep learning approach under standard, non-tuned hyperparameters for all models.
ai_summary: Deep neural networks have been successfully applied to structured clinical data with a good predictive performance . But their point predictions do not reflect an indication of confidence, which limits their trustworthiness in screening for genetic conditions .

title: The mediating role of artificial intelligence perception and creative idea generation in the impact of sustainable leadership on digital transformation and circular economy awareness.
abstract: Today, sustainable leadership is a strategic leadership approach that addresses environmental, social, and economic priorities from a holistic perspective while at the same time driving digital transformation processes. The research aims to explain how sustainable leaders mobilize organizational resources, technological infrastructure, and human creativity within the framework of Dynamic Capabilities Theory. The research was conducted on 456 white-collar employees working in small and medium-sized enterprises operating in Giresun, Kars, and Kırşehir provinces. The data collected by the convenience sampling method were analyzed using the PLS-SEM method with the SmartPLS 4.1.1 program. The analysis results show that sustainable leadership has significant and positive effects on perceptions of artificial intelligence, the generation of creative ideas, digital transformation, and awareness of the circular economy. It was found that the perception of artificial intelligence (AI) has a significant effect on both digital transformation and awareness of the circular economy. It was also determined that creative idea generation has significant effects on digital transformation and awareness of the circular economy. The results of the mediation analyses revealed a partial mediating role for all variables. The findings reveal that sustainable leadership is not limited to the environmental and social responsibility dimension and is a strategic element that directs digital transformation processes, shapes perceptions towards artificial intelligence, and encourages organizational creativity.

Results show that sustainable leadership has significant and positive effects on perceptions of artificial intelligence, the generation of creative ideas, digital transformation, and awareness of the circular economy .

title: Artificial intelligence for ophthalmic vessel segmentation: from multimodal imaging to clinical translation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based vessel segmentation converts color fundus photographs, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), structural OCT, and anterior-segment images into quantitative vascular biomarkers. Strong performance within individual datasets has not consistently yielded reliable clinical measurements because errors can arise during acquisition, anatomical preprocessing, vessel extraction, biomarker calculation, and deployment. This structured narrative review compares segmentation tasks involving retinal vascular trees, OCTA capillary plexuses, the structural choroid and choriocapillaris, macular neovascularization, corneal neovascularization, and conjunctival microvasculature. We assess modern architectures in relation to vessel geometry, severe foreground-background imbalance, scale variation, crossings, and susceptibility to artifacts. The methods considered include multiscale feature pyramids, deformable and directional operators, Transformers, state-space models, diffusion approaches, and foundation models. We organize the synthesis around five evaluation levels: pixel overlap, centerline recovery, vascular topology, biomarker agreement, and clinical actionability. Public fundus and OCTA datasets are catalogued with their acquisition and annotation characteristics, and gaps in public anterior-segment vessel benchmarks are discussed. Because devices, data splits, labels, and post-processing differ substantially, reported metrics are summarized without ranking studies against one another. The review distinguishes structural OCT choroidal vascularity index from OCTA choriocapillaris flow-deficit mapping, as well as true vessel segmentation from global hyperemia grading. Clinical translation will require ocular-magnification correction, quality control of retinal layers and projection artifacts, external testing across devices and populations, out-of-distribution rejection, DICOM/PACS interoperability, prospective impact studies, and regulation as software as a medical device. We conclude that clinical utility depends on an auditable pipeline that measures structural error, biomarker uncertainty, and failure states throughout the workflow.

Strong performance within individual datasets has not consistently yielded reliable clinical measurements . The methods considered include multiscale feature pyramids, deformable and directional operators .

title: Long COVID shows IL-1 pathway dysregulation without a discrete circulating biomarker signature.
abstract: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent and, often, disabling symptoms, yet its biological basis remains unclear. Multiple mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and persistence of SARS-CoV-2 components, have been proposed, although it is unknown whether these define distinct biological subtypes or overlapping processes. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 312 individuals, including 139 people with LC (PWLC), 99 COVID-19-recovered controls (both groups sampled a median of 8 months after primary SARS-CoV-2 infection), and 74 uninfected controls, from an unvaccinated population, thereby minimizing major sources of biological and epidemiological variability. Circulating immune and endothelial biomarkers and plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA were assessed, together with serological signatures associated with herpesvirus reactivation and SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral responses. Associations with symptom persistence were analyzed using multivariable models and machine learning approaches. Most soluble biomarker differences primarily distinguished previously infected individuals from uninfected controls rather than PWLC from recovered participants. Increased IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA) levels, together with reduced IL-1β/IL-1RA ratios, were the immune alterations most strongly associated with LC, while P-selectin was the endothelial marker showing a suggestive association with symptom persistence. Plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected at low and comparable frequencies in PWLC and recovered individuals, while Ct values tended to be lower among RNA-positive PWLC not reaching statistical difference. Epstein-Barr virus serological profiles were characterized by lower latency- and higher reactivation-associated responses in PWLC, whereas SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels were comparable between groups. Integrated biomarker profiles discriminated prior infection more effectively than LC status, and expansion to multimodal predictors did not clearly improve discrimination between PWLC and recovered participants. Overall, LC was associated with overlapping immune, endothelial, and virological alterations rather than discrete biomarker-defined subtypes.
ai_summary: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent and, often, disabling symptoms, yet its biological basis remains unclear . Multiple mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and persistence of SARS-CoV-2 components, have been proposed .

title: Environmental health literacy among oral healthcare professionals-a comparison across professional groups.
abstract: The present study aimed to assess environmental health literacy (EHL) among oral healthcare professionals and compare levels between dentists and non-dentist personnel in oral healthcare settings in Saudi Arabia. The study included dentists and non-dentist oral healthcare professionals (academicians, dental assistants, and allied health professionals) recruited using a convenience sampling approach. Data was collected using a structured questionnaire assessing four EHL domains: knowledge, attitude, confidence, and practice, along with demographic and professional characteristics. Responses were recorded on a 5-point Likert scale, and composite scores were calculated, with ≥70% considered a good literacy level. Data was analyzed using R Statistical Software, employing descriptive statistics, chi-square and t-tests, Spearman correlation, and multivariable logistic regression analyses. A total of 384 participants were included, of whom 258 were dentists and 126 were non-dentists. The overall literacy mean (SD) scores were comparable between dentists and non-dentists, with no statistically significant difference in overall literacy levels, at 70.5 (15.1) and 73.4 (15.8), respectively ( Overall, EHL was moderate among oral healthcare professionals, with notable differences in knowledge favoring non-dentists. Strengthening environmental health education and continuing professional development is essential to enhance literacy levels and promote sustainable oral healthcare practices.

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Three-Month Unplanned Readmission in Patients with Moderate-to-Severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Patients with moderate-to-severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) face a high risk of three-month unplanned readmission after discharge, yet early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging in clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting the risk and providing a reference for the subsequent development and updating of predictive tools. This single-center retrospective cohort study involved individuals with moderate-to-severe COPD from Tianjin Chest Hospital (January 2023 to January 2026). Participants were randomly split into a 70% training set and a 30% validation set. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression identified candidate predictors for model development. Six models were constructed: logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Naive Bayes (NB). Model performance was assessed through the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity (SEN), and specificity (SPE). Calibration was evaluated through calibration curves, and clinical utility via decision curve analysis (DCA). 299 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD were enrolled, and 59 (20%) experienced unplanned readmission within three months after discharge. Six ML models were compared, and the XGBoost model exhibited the best performance in the validation cohort, with an AUC of 0.809 (95% CI: 0.690-0.927), SEN of 0.750, and SPE of 0.826. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranked the key predictive factors in descending order: history of hospitalization in the past year, FEV1, history of coronary heart disease, and smoking history. XGBoost model showed promising performance in internal validation for predicting the risk of unplanned readmission among patients with moderate-to-severe COPD. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size, single-center design. Future studies should use prospective, multicenter data from diverse geographic regions to externally validate and update the model.
